messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: multiple customer streaming disconnects (SSE) + toolcall parse errors reported across edge nodes 3/4/7. Severity: P1. Initial alert at 2026-03-15T02:12:14Z.

satya: ack — I'm oncall. linking logs and starting triage. who saw repro on a client side? @ena?

ena: saw a spike of 502s hitting streaming-gateway in eu-west-1 ~02:08-02:14. Clients report `tool_call` payloads failing to parse. I have a local dump.

satya: ok, devon and marco for runtime infra please. lauren-cs add customer impact notes.

devon: jumping in. hypothesis: gateway's SSE relay is intermittently splitting frames, causing downstream parser to see truncated JSON -> parse error. collecting tcpdump + gateway logs now.

marco: infra note: we had a rolling kernel patch on node pool earlier but rolled back at 01:50. Not sure if related. Node pool 3 shows higher RST.

lauren-cs: customers impacted: PartnerA (prod), internal demo clusters for PartnerB, trial users in EU. PartnerA reported 12 failed sessions between 02:06-02:12, no data loss but user perceived timeouts.

satya: timeline we should assemble in this thread. i'll paste headers and ask ops-bot to attach logs.

ops-bot: Attaching s3://redwood-incident-logs/1959991234/ (gateway_logs.tar.gz, parse_traces.tar.gz, tcpdump-node3.pcap). Use `incident-bucket` creds.

ena: pasting minimal parse error snippet from gateway logs:

```
2026-03-15T02:09:11.341Z ERROR stream-parser: failed to parse tool_call payload: unexpected end of JSON input
request_id=rn-7b2e user_id=pa-122 model=redwood-large
raw_chunk="{\"tool_call\":{\"name\":\"search\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"error rate""
```

satya: that raw_chunk shows a truncated frame. do we have client-side chunking differences? @devon what's the SSE relay codepath for splitting frames?

devon: relay uses chunking with a 4k buffer flush. if upstream sends CRLF mid-json and our flush triggers, clients should reassemble. suspect issue is our health-check connection resets causing partial writes.

ena: tcpdump from node3 shows a `FIN` in the middle of the payload around 02:09:11. excerpt:

```
02:09:11.341 TCP 10.10.3.21:443 > 10.10.4.8:52344 [RST] Seq=... Ack=... Win=... Len=0
02:09:11.342 TCP 10.10.3.21:443 > 10.10.4.8:52344 [PSH, ACK] Seq=... Len=512
```

marco: interesting — RSTs correlate with the kernel patch rollback window earlier. Could be a lingering netstack bug on that node pool.

satya: action items: 
- devon to patch relay to buffer until full SSE event boundary when possible (hotfix)
- marco to cordon node3 and move traffic to node4
- ena to extract full parse traces and annotate which clients saw truncated frames
- lauren-cs to send customer update

devon: starting hotfix branch now. quick mitigation: increase relay keepalive and enable `--sse-boundary-safe` in config. applying to canary in eu-west-1.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary (relay-fix) -> gateway-eu-west-1-canary. Deploy ID: dpl-195999-01

ena: attaching annotated parse_traces.tar.gz/partnerA/session_6692.trace (see lines with `incomplete_event` flag)

satya: can we get a quick runbook for on-call handoff in case we need to escalate? I’ll be on for next 60m then hand to devon.

devon: yes. if errors persist after canary (10m window), escalate to infra oncall @marco and open customer umbrella page. I'll also collect a golden trace with `tcpdump -w /tmp/golden.pcap host 10.10.4.8`.

lauren-cs: Customer update draft:

"PartnerA - we observed intermittent streaming interruptions impacting live tool-calls. Our engineering team is actively mitigating; temporary routing changes and a hotfix are being deployed. No user data lost. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

satya: good. marking in-thread hypotheses:
1) netstack/kernel rollback caused mid-payload TCP resets -> truncated SSE frames -> parser errors
2) relay buffer flush policy edge-case when CRLF in payload -> splits JSON across SSE writes
3) client library incompatibility with fragmented SSE frames causing mis-reassembly

ena: i found one client retry pattern for PartnerB that re-sends partial payloads — adds weight to #3 for some clients.

marco: cordoning node3 now. shifting 20% traffic off node3 to node4. ETA 3m.

ops-bot: Node3 cordon complete. Traffic shift started.

devon: canary shows 0 parse errors in last 6 minutes. rolling to eu-west-1 pool.

ops-bot: Rollout to eu-west-1 started: relay-fix -> pool-3/4/7. Monitor window 15m.

lauren-cs: sending partner-facing update now. pinging partners slack channel.

satya: after rollout, we'll collect a post-mortem. for the RCA thread we need: timeline, root cause, mitigations, long-term fix, customer impact numbers, rollout notes.

ena: attaching timeline snippet (times UTC) and a small table in comment.

```
02:06:22 - first spike of 502s observed (PartnerA)
02:08:55 - incident-bot alert threshold crossed
02:09:11 - parse error spikes + RSTs on node3
02:12:30 - cordon node3 initiated
02:20:10 - canary deploy applied
02:28:40 - rollout complete, error rate normalized
```

devon: follow-ups for RCA: add unit tests for SSE boundary reassembly, consider upstream backpressure signals, and add better metrics (incomplete_event) on gateway side.

satya: handoff: I'm wrapping; devon you're on for next shift. please capture any late failure and start the formal RCA doc under /incidents/postmortems.

devon: ack. I'll create the postmortem draft and include the linked logs and hypotheses. thanks all.

marco: closing temporary mitigations: node3 remains cordoned until kernel patch validated. rolling reboots deferred.

lauren-cs: customers notified. PartnerA responded: "thanks, appreciate quick action".

ops-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. closing alert stream. Incident ID: INC-1959991234

satya: final note: set severity->P1->P2 transition after postmortem acceptance. good work team :raised_hands:
